title: How to get stock balance having inventory dimension in server script?

posts.cooked:
x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', 
 item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001',
 warehouse='Finished Goods - T'
)
print(x)

output: 1471.0

with inventory dimension:

x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', 
 item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001',
 warehouse='Finished Goods - T',
 inventory_dimensions_dict={'customer': 'test'}
)
print(x)

output: 1471.0

Actually, I noticed that get_stock_balance does not handle inventory dimensions correctly. It simply fetches the qty_after_transaction from the Stock Ledger Entry, which is why you are still seeing 1471.0 even after passing the inventory dimension.

FE

  • If you make a Stock Entry for Item A with a quantity of 1000 in Warehouse B, the SLE will show Qty Change = 1000 and Qty After Transaction = 1000.

  • Then, if you make another entry for the same item and warehouse but with an inventory dimension (say, Customer C) and a quantity of 471, the new SLE will show Qty Change = 471 and Qty After Transaction = 1471.

This is why get_stock_balance always returns 1471.0, as it does not filter by the inventory dimension.

Are you sure? In my most recent testing I found that it now does at least return dimensioned quantity correctly, but there is no way to get undimensioned quantity. Can you post a video or screenshot? Also, I found that the Inventory Dimension Validation Logic doesn’t make sense, and I can’t fix it because there is no function that returns undimensioned stock of an item.

What I mean is that when you create a material receipt with qty 100 of item1 with dimension x and after that create a material issue for qty 50 of item1 without dimension, the system will not throw a validation error saying there is no undimensioned stock. Instead, it does some very weird thing where undimensioned stock of item1 is now -50 (even though negative stock is disabled) and dimensioned stock remains 100.

I have contacted Support multiple times about this, but they claim it works as intended because -50 + 100 = 50, lmao.

By the way, this behavior causes another issue where sometimes 0-stock items show up in the balance report because the valuation rate somehow becomes negative. Again, this is with default settings.

In short, Inventory Dimension is basically unusable this way. The only workaround is to make the dimension mandatory, but this limits the flexibility of the feature a lot. My suggestion would be to develop Inventory Dimensions further so they are part of the Bin doctype (I even offered to pay for the feature) or at least validate undimensioned stock correctly if that is too large of a change.

Nevermind my last answer it still does not return the correct qty. When testing this i made the mistake to not check for multiple consecutive stock entries with different dimension values which caused exactly the one i checked to accidentally be correct because it was the first stock entry and for that item/dimension value combination stock never left inventory after that. Bottom line is it returns the wrong qty, i wrote some utility functions that actually return the correct qty in my custom app, if someone needs it hit me up.
